question: Does the times-through-the-order penalty justify pulling starters before the 3rd time?
answer: For an average starter, yes. 3rd time: +.022 wOBA vs 1st (same pitcher), .339 vs relievers .323.
findings: Within pitcher-season: 2nd time +.013 (CI +.011 to +.016), 3rd time +.022 (CI +.020 to +.025) wOBA vs 1st.
Pitch count adds nothing: -.004 (CI -.012 to +.004) per 100 pitches; 3rd time stays +.025.
Jump at batter 19: +.017 (SE .003) in 2015-19, +.000 (SE .003) in 2020-25, a smooth rise instead.
Batter-adjusted wOBA: starters 1st time .321, 3rd time .339; relievers inn. 6+ .323 (n=664,061).
method: OLS on PA wOBA with pitcher-season fixed effects, batter-season wOBA, platoon and home; SE clustered by game. Survivors to the 3rd time are pitchers having better days, so the penalty is if anything understated.
data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2015-2025 regular season, 1,109,963 starter PAs (1st-3rd time), 24,958 games. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).
split_check: 3rd-time penalty +.024 in 2015-19 and +.020 in 2020-25; discrete jumps only in 2015-19.
